extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: TravelPlanner is a planning benchmark that focuses on travel planning, a common real-world planning scenario. It provides a rich sandbox environment with around four million data entries crawled from the Internet that can be accessed via six tools. It includes 1,225 meticulously curated diverse user queries along with their reference plans, each imposing a different combination of constraints. The benchmark evaluates whether language agents can develop flexible travel plans by collecting information via diverse tools and making decisions while satisfying environment, commonsense, and hard constraints.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su (Fudan University, The Ohio State University, The Pennsylvania State University, Meta AI)
extraction.citeAs: Xie, J., Zhang, K., Chen, J., Zhu, T., Lou, R., Tian, Y., Xiao, Y., & Su, Y. (2024). TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents. arXiv:2402.01622v4 [cs.CL].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset environment is built from publicly available Internet data. The original data for each tool is sourced from publicly available Internet data, which was then modified (adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values) to suit benchmark requirements and avoid data contamination. FlightSearch data is sourced from the Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset, spanning from 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01. DistanceMatrix data is obtained via the Google Distance Matrix API. RestaurantSearch data is sourced from the Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset. AttractionSearch data is gathered using the Google Places API. AccommodationSearch data is obtained from the Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset. A static and closed sandbox environment was created for consistent and unbiased evaluations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: FlightSearch: Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset (Combined_Flights_2022.csv). DistanceMatrix: Google Distance Matrix API. RestaurantSearch: Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset. AttractionSearch: Google Places API. AccommodationSearch: Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: FlightSearch: Fields extracted include FlightDate, DepTime, ArrTime, ActualElapsedTime, Distance, OriginCityName, and DestCityName. Price was generated by multiplying Distance by a random factor ranging from 0.2 to 0.5. DistanceMatrix: Price for self-driving calculated by multiplying Distance by 1; taxi price by multiplying Distance by 0.15. RestaurantSearch: Restaurant Name and Average Cost extracted; restaurants randomly assigned to various cities; cuisine categories randomly assigned. AttractionSearch: Name, Address, Phone, Website, Latitude, and Longitude retained; results stored in a standardized database. AccommodationSearch: NAME, room type, price, minimum nights, review rate number, and maximum occupancy extracted; items randomly assigned to cities; random room rules assigned. Original data was modified by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to avoid data contamination.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A static and closed sandbox environment was created. Data was stored in fixed databases to ensure consistency and reliability. Query construction involved randomly choosing departure city, destination, and date range, then adjusting travel duration (3, 5, or 7 days) and number of hard constraints to create different complexity levels. Budgets were re-calibrated using costs from human-annotated plans to replace heuristic-generated budgets. Natural language queries were generated using GPT-4 based on structured JSON elements.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 20 graduate students were invited to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries. A plan is deemed eligible only if it meets all the constraints outlined in the evaluation script. This process resulted in 1,225 validated query-plan pairs. Annotators were paid an average of $0.80 for each plan annotated. The authors performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found. Budgets were re-calibrated using costs from corresponding human-annotated plans.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control involved authors performing a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found. Budgets were re-calibrated using costs from corresponding human-annotated plans to replace initial heuristic-generated budgets, which might be too high, thus reducing the number of feasible plans. Multiple stages of human verification ensured high quality and the presence of at least one feasible solution per query. On average, human annotators took approximately 12 minutes to manually annotate a plan.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors will release evaluation scripts to foster innovation and aid the development of new methods. Use of evaluation feedback in the training set is encouraged (e.g., reinforcement learning). Any form of cheating in the validation and test sets is strictly prohibited to uphold fairness and reliability.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: TravelPlanner aims to provide an effective benchmark for complex planning in future research. Some of the data in the TravelPlanner environment is derived from publicly available data on the Internet, and the content involved does not represent the authors' viewpoints. The benchmark is intended as a catalyst for future research to enhance agents' performance in increasingly complex scenarios, hill-climbing towards human-level cognitive capabilities. Language agents could potentially help automate tedious planning tasks for humans.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The commonsense evaluation criteria are based on the authors' consensus, and the authors acknowledge that everyone's definition of commonsense may be different. Additional discussions are encouraged to enrich the commonsense dimension for a more thorough evaluation. Restaurant data was randomly assigned to cities, and accommodation room rules were randomly assigned, which may not reflect real-world distributions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark uses a static and closed sandbox environment, which may not capture the full variability of real-world travel planning. The dataset is based on data from 2022 (March 2022 dates), which may limit temporal generalizability. The commonsense constraints are based on authors' consensus and may not capture all cultural or individual variations in commonsense. The benchmark focuses specifically on travel planning within the United States.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of language agents' tool-use and complex multi-constraint planning capabilities. The training set (45 query-plan pairs) can be used for training or fine-tuning, including reinforcement learning techniques. The validation set (180 queries) and test set (1,000 queries) are intended for evaluation. The benchmark is designed to assess whether agents can generate feasible solutions facing various objectives (constraints) in a real-world planning scenario.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4-Turbo (used for extracting key components from natural language plans into structured format for evaluation; also used for generating natural language queries from structured JSON)
